- A threshold for “significant” events: consolidated pre‑tax losses exceeding $150 million from an event occurring in the current year [Source 6][Source 8].  
- Specific catastrophe exposures that could generate large losses:  
  • Hurricanes Milton and Helene (2024) [Source 6]  
  • A cyclone and floods in New Zealand and a hailstorm in Italy (2023) [Source 6]  
  • Hurricane Ian and floods in Australia (2022) [Source 6]

- Foreign‑currency transaction gains or losses arising from the remeasurement of non‑U.S.‑dollar‑denominated assets and liabilities can also “significantly affect our periodic underwriting results” [Source 6][Source 8].  
- Full risk retention: Berkshire “generally do not retrocede the risks we assume,” meaning it retains the underwriting risk on its policies [Source 6].  
- Underwriting of retroactive reinsurance and periodic‑payment annuity contracts creates large up‑front premiums with long‑tail claim obligations, producing underwriting losses over the claim‑settlement periods [Source 4][Source 8].
